title: Security cameras captured a bright fireball over Springfield, Missouri
excerpt: Greene County security cameras captured a bright fireball streaking across the Springfield sky during the annual Taurid meteor shower last Friday night.
content:
SPRINGFIELD, Mo. – A bright fireball streaking across the night sky over Springfield was caught on two highway department security cameras, providing a dramatic view of a celestial event that lit up the region.

The videos, released Tuesday by the Greene County Highway Department, show a bright streak racing across the sky at approximately 8:40 p.m. on Friday, Nov. 13.

County officials believe the object was likely part of the annual Taurid meteor shower, which is known for producing slow-moving, exceptionally bright meteors, often referred to as “fireballs.”

In a post on social media, Greene County officials said the object was “likely part of the Taurid meteor shower, known for slow, bright fireballs.”

The Taurid meteor shower occurs each fall and is famous among skywatchers for producing bright meteors that can remain visible longer than typical shooting stars. While the shower typically generates fewer meteors than some other annual displays, it is known for producing particularly impressive fireballs.

The security camera footage shows the object briefly illuminating the night sky before disappearing from view.

For those hoping to catch a glimpse of similar celestial displays, the Taurid meteor shower remains active through late November.
